sections.html:
Putnam County had 22,047 residents at the 2020 census and an estimated 23,722 in July 2025. Eatonton levies its own city tax, and the tax commissioner runs county billing from putnamgatax.com.

The market skews older. Residents 65 and over make up 27.1% of the population, and households average just 2.17 people. A typical owner-occupied home is valued at $249,300, rent is about $1,002 a month, and the middle household income is $72,096. Owners live in 80.9% of housing units, and monthly housing costs run $1,522 with a loan and $485 without. Building permits numbered 98 in 2025. The average commute is 31.1 minutes.

The county has 14,017 housing units but 10,435 households, a gap of roughly 3,600. Not every property is someone's legal residence, so ask the assessors whether yours carries a homestead exemption before you promise a buyer a particular tax figure. For an owner on a fixed income, an unpaid tax bill and a deferred repair list are the two problems most likely to push a sale.

sections.h2: Which Putnam County office does what?
sections.html:
The tax commissioner collects, and the Board of Tax Assessors values.

  • Tax Commissioner: collects property, timber and heavy duty equipment tax. Payments can be made on the website, by phone with a card, by mail, or at the office.
  • Tax Assessors: (706) 485-6376, with parcel records at qpublic.net/ga/putnam.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: intangible tax and deed copies, in the courthouse.
  • Marine equipment specialist: an assessor staffer who handles boats.

The commissioner also hands out a Taxpayer Brochure that walks through returns, exemptions and appeals. County information is at putnamcountyga.us.

Putnam County billing calendar
Bill typeBills mailedDue date
Real and personal propertyBy October 1December 1
Mobile homeBy February 1April 1

A mobile home decal is no longer required.

Interest starts accruing one day late, then posts again each month on the 1st. The rate is the prime rate in force at the start of the year plus 3%. At 120 days a 5% penalty arrives, with another 5% for each further 120-day period, to a ceiling of 20%. A mobile home pays a flat 10% beginning the day after its due date.

Homesteaded property owing less than $500 skips the 90-day penalty. The commissioner mails each bill to the owner, never to the lender.

sections.h2: If I sell mid-year, who gets the Putnam County bill?
sections.html:
The seller of record on January 1 gets the first bill. Once a new deed is recorded, the commissioner sends the buyer a copy as well.

Read your closing papers or ask the closing attorney who owes the money. Make sure the contract and the settlement statement spell out the year's tax, whether closing lands before or after December 1.

Boats follow the same January 1 logic. Sell one and the fall bill still comes unless the assessors' marine specialist is told. Only accounts totaling $20,000 or more in marine equipment get a bill.

sections.h2: Appeals and ways to lower a bill
sections.html:
Your first appeal goes to the assessors, who may revise the value and mail a second notice. If they hold at the same number, the file is forwarded for a hearing. An arbitrator is another option, with 45 days from the notice date to ask for it.

  • Homestead: own and occupy on January 1, file at the assessors, and get the paper in before April 1.
  • Age 70: owners who reach it can request an extra homestead exemption.
  • Relief grant: the 2023 state grant cut assessed value by $18,000 on homesteaded property, and the commissioner says it returns for tax year 2026. Rentals and non-homesteaded property were not eligible.
  • Refund: a claim for tax wrongly collected has to begin within three years of the payment date.

The final step in a dispute is Superior Court, started by written notice to the assessors.

The formula starts at 40% of fair market value, subtracts exemptions, then applies the millage rate. The county commissioners, the school board, the City of Eatonton and the State of Georgia each set a rate, with one mill worth $1 per $1,000 of taxable value.

The money pays for schools and county government, public buildings, bridges and roads, courts, the jail and law enforcement, fire protection, and public health and sanitation. The assessors take real estate returns during the first three months of the year.

sections.h2: What happens if tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
A FiFa can be recorded 30 days after the commissioner sends a 30-day notice. Because it is a public lien record, it can reach credit bureaus once a bill is more than 90 days late.

The tax sale is generally annual, held at the courthouse on the first Tuesday of July. Registration opens at 9 am, and bidders must show photo ID, pay in certified funds and settle the same day by 4 pm. There is no electronic bidding, and owners with delinquent county accounts cannot register. The list is published in The Eatonton Messenger and on Georgia Public Notice.

Paying the commissioner's payoff at closing keeps your property off that list.

A little groundwork keeps the closing on schedule. Look up your parcel at qpublic.net/ga/putnam and confirm the owner name, the assessed value and whether a homestead exemption shows. If the exemption is missing and you lived there on January 1, the assessors can tell you what the form needs and whether the April 1 cutoff is still ahead.

  • Pay or schedule the current bill. The commissioner accepts payment on the website, by card over the phone, by mail or in person.
  • Gather the tax bill for the year, since the buyer's lender and the closing attorney will ask for it.
  • Check the settlement statement draft for the line that covers the year's tax.
  • Tell your mortgage servicer about the sale if it pays the bill from escrow, because the commissioner mails bills to the owner and not to the lender.

None of this takes long, and each item removes a reason for a buyer to delay or ask for a lower price.

Ask the commissioner for a written payoff and give it to the closing attorney, who will subtract it from your proceeds. The figure moves each month because interest posts on the 1st, so request it close to the closing date.

  1. Confirm which year's bill is open and whether the buyer or you agreed to cover it.
  2. Ask whether a FiFa has been recorded and what clears it.
  3. If the city of Eatonton levies tax on your parcel, request that balance too.
  4. For a boat or other equipment on the rolls, tell the assessors about the sale.

A cash buyer can close around an inherited deed, a repair list or a stalled listing. The tax is still paid out of your proceeds at the table, so you leave the closing with the account clear and no list publication ahead of you.

faqs.q: What date are Putnam County taxes due?
faqs.a: December 1 for real estate and business personal property. Mobile home taxes are due April 1.

faqs.q: Does Putnam County auction delinquent properties?
faqs.a: Yes. It generally holds one sale a year, on the first Tuesday in July at the courthouse, with in-person bidding only.

faqs.q: Who owes tax if my Putnam County house sells in mid-year?
faqs.a: The January 1 owner is billed first, and the buyer later receives a copy. Your closing attorney and contract decide who pays.

faqs.q: How is the Putnam County late penalty set?
faqs.a: Interest runs at the January prime rate plus 3%. A 5% penalty follows at day 120 and repeats every 120 days until 20%.

faqs.q: Where do I find a Putnam County parcel record?
faqs.a: At qpublic.net/ga/putnam, or by calling the assessors at (706) 485-6376.
